steps.observation: You have 300 seconds. Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper.

steps.action:
Elias checked his pocket watch: 300 seconds until the storm’s heart struck the craggy shore. As lighthouse keeper of Gull’s Point, he had faced furious seas before—but never one this sudden, this violent.

Seconds ticked away as he climbed the spiral stairs, boots echoing on worn stone. At the lantern room’s door, he found the oil reservoir leaking, the wick charred beyond use. Lightning split the sky, momentarily illuminating an anxious fishing trawler dancing on the waves below. Those fishermen were counting on his beam.

He took a deep breath. One hundred fifty seconds left.

Elias ripped open his leather satchel, pulling free a spare wick and a sealed flask of lamp oil. His gloved hands trembled as he emptied fresh oil into the reservoir. Sparks from a flint striker lit the new wick with a stubborn flare. He adjusted the lens shutters, praying the mechanism wouldn’t jam.

Eighty seconds. The wind howled through a broken window frame, rattling glass. The trawler’s lights bobbed like lost fireflies in the dark swell.

Thirty seconds. Elias cranked the rotation gear until the great Fresnel lens glowed, refracting light into a steady, piercing beam. He forced the hand crank faster; the light swung outward in measured arcs.

Ten seconds. A colossal wave smashed against the cliff, rattling the foundation.

Five… four… three… two…

The beam found the trawler. A shout rose from its deck, faint but hopeful.

One second later, Elias exhaled. The storm had arrived—but so had salvation. As thunder rolled and rain battered the shores, the lighthouse keeper stood guard, lamp unwavering, faith unbroken.
